michael-moore.name: Michael Moore
michael-moore.reference: Author-led investigative satire; Roger & Me as a reference, rather than a universal documentary template.
michael-moore.mechanism: A public claim becomes a concrete, often absurd encounter.
michael-moore.prerequisites: Contradictory statements with dates, a specific affected person or place, and preferably an actual encounter.
michael-moore.selection: Build selects by claim, test and consequence. Prefer a revealing exchange, procedural obstacle or ordinary detail over unrelated shots of wealth or suffering.
michael-moore.framing: Keep locations legible enough to establish who has access, who waits and who controls the encounter. A crop should reveal an observation, not manufacture embarrassment.
michael-moore.rhythm: Try claim → literal test → unforeseen answer → consequence. Place the comic reversal after the audience understands the premise; preserve the subject's qualifying words.
michael-moore.sound: Let a revealing answer play clearly. Test either an ironic cue or unscored location sound at the reversal; choose the version that makes the contradiction understandable.
michael-moore.typography: Show the exact claim and its source briefly. Use typography to distinguish quotation from editorial commentary; do not invent a Moore-wide font.
michael-moore.exceptions: Keep quote integrity. Treat bans on piano, slow motion and neutral passages as optional tonal choices. A stated viewpoint does not require commentary over every image.
michael-moore.evaluation: Make a 25-second sequence from a claim and a documented outcome. A viewer should identify the contradiction without the narrator explaining the joke.
michael-moore.failureMode: A sarcastic narrator over generic archive has attitude but no encounter.

evidence.summary: In his TIFF speech, Moore argues for entertainment, humor and a filmmaker's point of view. He specifically rejects routine illustrative images when a more revealing scene can carry the idea.

sources.title: 13 Rules for Making Documentary Films
sources.author_publisher: Michael Moore; TIFF speech, reprinted by Reader Supported News
sources.supports: Entertainment, humor, authorial perspective and resistance to documentary cliches.

errol-morris.name: Errol Morris
errol-morris.reference: Investigative interview and constructed-image nonfiction; The Thin Blue Line is one reference.
errol-morris.mechanism: Testimony and recurring images expose uncertainty instead of closing it too soon.
errol-morris.prerequisites: Substantial interview answers, corroborating records and, where appropriate, clearly identified reconstructions.
errol-morris.selection: Choose an answer with a precise assertion and a detail another source can test. Keep the speaker's reasoning, hesitation or self-correction when it changes the meaning.
errol-morris.framing: For new interviews, use a consistent intimate eyeline and simple visual field. For reconstructions, photograph evidentiary details whose differing versions can be compared.
errol-morris.rhythm: Return to the same detail when testimony changes. Let each recurrence add or contradict information; avoid repeating a shot merely to seem mysterious.
errol-morris.sound: Try a recurring musical figure that remains unresolved across competing accounts. Keep intelligibility and the speaker's unforced cadence ahead of the score.
errol-morris.typography: Identify document origin and reconstruction status. Give competing versions consistent visual treatment so typography does not silently certify one.
errol-morris.exceptions: Replace blanket prohibitions on questions, narration, handheld and drums with an inquiry-specific design. Stylization requires factual discipline; it does not license presenting an imagined event as observed.
errol-morris.evaluation: Cut two conflicting accounts around one recurring object in 30 seconds. The viewer should state what remains uncertain and what evidence could resolve it.
errol-morris.failureMode: A direct-to-camera interview and a brooding loop do not by themselves create an investigation.

evidence.summary: Morris rejects the idea that any visual method guarantees truth. His account of The Thin Blue Line's music also shows score being used during development, not merely added as atmosphere after picture lock.

sources.title: Errol Morris interview
sources.author_publisher: The Believer; hosted by Errol Morris
sources.supports: Stylization and documentary truth; method does not guarantee truth.

ken-burns.name: Ken Burns
ken-burns.reference: Historical archive documentary; attention directed within still images and testimony.
ken-burns.mechanism: An image changes meaning as its context and human stakes become visible.
ken-burns.prerequisites: High-resolution photographs with useful internal detail, reliable dates and first-person records.
ken-burns.selection: Find photographs containing both an initial point of attention and a consequential wider context. Collect letters or testimony that individualize the event without exceeding what the record establishes.
ken-burns.framing: Design a start frame, discovery and resting frame. Preserve enough resolution for the largest crop; hold still when the photograph's composition already communicates the point.
ken-burns.rhythm: Move or reveal on a change of meaning in the testimony. Alternate a personal detail with the broader historical situation rather than applying the same zoom to every still.
ken-burns.sound: Build a small thematic palette before final assembly. Let music recur with changed context; give testimony space and use environmental sound selectively, without implying it is original recording.
ken-burns.typography: Use discreet dates and source labels. Separate editorial titles from archival lettering; avoid an obligatory sepia treatment or decorative period type.
ken-burns.exceptions: Keep disciplined image motion and historical specificity. Remove unsupported career-wide bans on drums, rapid cutting or first-person passages; these should be reference-specific choices.
ken-burns.evaluation: Make a 20-second still-image sequence whose final framing changes the opening interpretation. Test once without movement: retain motion only if it improves the discovery.
ken-burns.failureMode: Continuous slow zooms without a designed reveal create movement but little historical insight.

evidence.summary: Burns describes developing music alongside the writing and archive search. He gives a concrete example of a photograph whose wider framing transforms an apparently ordinary domestic scene into something chilling.

sources.title: No Longer Just Wallpaper: Archival Footage Can Inform and Shape Your Film's Story
sources.evidence_type: Craft reporting with direct Burns interview
sources.supports: Music developed alongside script and archive; reframing stills changes meaning.

werner-herzog.name: Werner Herzog
werner-herzog.reference: Essayistic nonfiction and subjective encounter; distinguish poetic narration from factual claims.
werner-herzog.mechanism: A concrete observation opens a larger, unsettling question.
werner-herzog.prerequisites: An unusual real encounter, behavior or environment with enough duration to observe it.
werner-herzog.selection: Seek behavior that resists an immediate explanation: a repeated task, an obsession, an indifferent landscape or an unexpected gesture. Avoid stock imagery chosen only because it looks bleak.
werner-herzog.framing: Keep the relationship between person and environment visible. Hold long enough for something specific to happen or for the viewer to revise an initial interpretation.
werner-herzog.rhythm: Try observation → restrained question → return to observation. End before the narration exhausts the image's possibilities; use duration as inquiry rather than as a fixed minimum.
werner-herzog.sound: Collect the environment as a distinct dramatic presence. Test a musical passage only where it changes the scale of the thought; preserve a contrasting stretch of unscored sound.
werner-herzog.typography: Supply essential factual context plainly. Maps and labels are permitted when needed; the image's ambiguity should not depend on withholding basic facts.
werner-herzog.exceptions: Replace bans on maps, interviews, lower thirds and quick sequences with a preference for experiential evidence. Mark imagined language as interpretation and preserve documentary provenance.
werner-herzog.evaluation: Build a 25-second encounter with one observational sentence and one open question. Viewers should describe the actual behavior before discussing the larger theme.
werner-herzog.failureMode: Grandiose narration over interchangeable landscapes substitutes a persona for discovery.

evidence.summary: Herzog's essays argue for a form of cinematic truth beyond literal description. They support a subjective artistic position, not a reliable recipe of slow shots, accent imitation or unrestricted factual invention.

sources.title: Texts by Werner Herzog: On the Absolute, the Sublime, and Ecstatic Truth
sources.supports: Distinction between literal fact and subjective or poetic experience.

frederick-wiseman.name: Frederick Wiseman
frederick-wiseman.reference: Institutional observational documentary; At Berkeley and Boxing Gym provide concrete editing references.
frederick-wiseman.mechanism: Procedures and relationships reveal how an institution works.
frederick-wiseman.prerequisites: Complete interactions, intelligible location audio, procedural coverage and context for the participants' roles.
frederick-wiseman.selection: Find a task with a decision, negotiation or change in authority. Favor exchanges that show the rules operating over isolated emotional reactions.
frederick-wiseman.framing: Preserve who speaks to whom and what each person is doing. Include spatial or procedural context before relying on a revealing close-up.
frederick-wiseman.rhythm: Compress repetition while maintaining the logic of the exchange. Join scenes because their procedures, power relations or sounds converse; retain ambiguity where the institution itself produces it.
frederick-wiseman.sound: Use location sound to carry continuity or connect different activities. Avoid adding sounds that misrepresent what happened; silence and room tone can also separate institutional spaces.
frederick-wiseman.typography: Keep administrative context available in restrained labels when necessary. A title may orient viewers without telling them which participant is right.
frederick-wiseman.exceptions: An observational reference can prefer no explanatory narrator or added score. Remove the claim that statements cannot be shortened: ethical compression and constructed continuity are central editorial decisions.
frederick-wiseman.evaluation: Cut a 30-second procedural scene. A viewer should identify the task, the decision-maker and the unresolved tension without voiceover.
frederick-wiseman.failureMode: Long shots of an institution with no intelligible process produce opacity rather than observation.

evidence.summary: Wiseman describes reducing a lengthy class to a much shorter constructed scene and linking Boxing Gym sequences with overlapping location sound. Observational presentation therefore coexists with substantial editorial construction.

sources.title: The Choice and Order: An Interview with Frederick Wiseman
sources.supports: Constructed continuity, compression and sound bridges in At Berkeley and Boxing Gym.

humphrey-jennings.name: Humphrey Jennings
humphrey-jennings.reference: Poetic wartime documentary; distinguish Listen to Britain from the narrated Words for Battle.
humphrey-jennings.mechanism: Sound connects separate lives into a larger social picture.
humphrey-jennings.prerequisites: Everyday activities with useful sound, contrasting social spaces and reliable historical identification.
humphrey-jennings.selection: Pair work, leisure and public ritual through a shared action or sound. Look for social difference within the connection, rather than smoothing every image into national unity.
humphrey-jennings.framing: Retain enough of each environment to make its social role visible. Human activity and the surrounding space should both contribute to the association.
humphrey-jennings.rhythm: Try introducing a sound in one place and continuing it over another. Return to its source after the connection becomes clear; vary the distance between sonic and visual links.
humphrey-jennings.sound: Plan the sequence from listening relationships: machinery, footsteps, broadcast, communal music, quiet. Treat recorded music within the scene differently from an added emotional bed.
humphrey-jennings.typography: Use contextual dates or locations where archive alone is insufficient. Title design should support the chosen historical execution, not force all work into one typography rule.
humphrey-jennings.exceptions: The prohibition on commentary is contradicted by Words for Battle. Keep sound-led association as a strong option, while allowing visual links and different forms across the career.
humphrey-jennings.evaluation: Make a 25-second sequence connecting three spaces through one sound. Viewers should identify both the connection and how the spaces differ.
humphrey-jennings.failureMode: A patriotic music bed over assorted archive erases the specific relationships that make the montage meaningful.

evidence.summary: BFI's account distinguishes Jennings's different forms and identifies Words for Battle's narration. Listen to Britain is also a collaboration with Stewart McAllister; its achievement should not be reduced to a sole-director visual preset.
evidence.basis: Institutional analysis and primary work record

sources.title: Where to begin with Humphrey Jennings
sources.supports: Listen to Britain, McAllister collaboration and narrated Words for Battle.

sources.title: Listen to Britain
sources.author_publisher: BFI Player; Humphrey Jennings and Stewart McAllister
sources.supports: Primary work and collaborator attribution.

lemmino.name: LEMMiNO
lemmino.reference: Researched mystery and spatial explanation; the book-depository episode is a bounded reference.
lemmino.mechanism: A confusing event becomes a set of inspectable claims, positions and uncertainties.
lemmino.prerequisites: A source-backed timeline and a diagram or spatial model whose known and uncertain elements can be distinguished.
lemmino.selection: Organize material by the question each item answers. Prefer records that establish time, position, visibility or contradiction; retain unresolved alternatives in the research ledger.
lemmino.framing: Use a stable diagram orientation before moving the virtual camera. Show the entire relationship, then isolate the relevant line of sight or location.
lemmino.rhythm: Introduce one question, establish the model, test the claim, then update the model. Move into a new chapter only when the current uncertainty has changed.
lemmino.sound: Try a restrained recurring texture with distinct section changes. Reduce musical activity during dense evidence; reserve an accent for a real evidentiary turn.
lemmino.typography: Give known, inferred and unknown information different line or fill treatments with a legend. Label locations and dates consistently; avoid visual precision unsupported by the sources.
lemmino.exceptions: Remove automatic still motion, compulsory map/date beats and blanket stock-footage bans. Require a reason for each movement and a source for each apparently precise diagram.
lemmino.evaluation: Create a 30-second explanation of one line-of-sight claim. A viewer should distinguish the measured geometry from assumptions without reading the research notes.
lemmino.failureMode: Photorealistic reconstruction can make weak evidence appear more certain than it is.

evidence.summary: LEMMiNO's episode page provides an extensive source apparatus and music credits; the FAQ documents production tools. These establish a research and production foundation, but do not establish mandatory movement on every still or a fixed chapter-map formula.

sources.title: The Kennedy Assassination: Inside the Book Depository
sources.supports: Detailed evidence apparatus, episode scope and music credits.

sources.title: FAQ
sources.supports: Tools and music sourcing; does not establish universal shot or font rules.

ridley-scott.name: Ridley Scott
ridley-scott.reference: Commercial world-building; avoid collapsing the full feature-film career into the 1984 advertisement.
ridley-scott.mechanism: A believable visual world makes a brief action feel consequential.
ridley-scott.prerequisites: Environment, costume, lighting and action coverage designed to belong to the same world.
ridley-scott.selection: Choose shots that establish a rule of the world, a figure acting within it and the consequence. Reject spectacular inserts that introduce incompatible architecture, light or social context.
ridley-scott.framing: Plan foreground, subject and depth separately. Establish motivated light sources and material texture; choose camera stability according to the action rather than a permanent prohibition.
ridley-scott.rhythm: Open with enough orientation for the decisive action to register. Use closer details to clarify intent, then widen for consequence; reserve an accelerated burst for a meaningful rupture.
ridley-scott.sound: Build the world with machinery, crowd, weather or other specific ambience before enlarging it with music. Give a decisive action a distinctive acoustic signature.
ridley-scott.typography: Design the final title or product reveal as part of the environment's visual logic. Set its duration by recognition and message length, not a universal three-second cap.
ridley-scott.exceptions: Replace bans on handheld, daylight, humor and particular music genres with reference-specific choices. A dark grade cannot substitute for production design.
ridley-scott.evaluation: In 20 seconds, establish one environmental rule and show an action that breaks it. Viewers should understand the rupture without a premise card.
ridley-scott.failureMode: Unrelated smoky wides and glossy close-ups suggest scale without a coherent world.

evidence.summary: Scott's DGA interview connects his drawing and design background with practical camera experience. He explicitly includes handheld among the methods he used while operating commercial shoots, contradicting the harness's blanket exclusion.

sources.title: Man of Vision
sources.author_publisher: Directors Guild of America; Ridley Scott interview
sources.supports: Drawing, production design and hands-on commercial camerawork, including handheld.

spike-jonze.name: Spike Jonze
spike-jonze.reference: Performance-led imaginative advertising; Welcome Home is the principal production reference.
spike-jonze.mechanism: An ordinary emotional state becomes a physical transformation.
spike-jonze.prerequisites: A committed performer, repeatable choreography and space that can transform practically or through planned effects.
spike-jonze.selection: Start with a legible bodily state: tiredness, hesitation or release. Choose actions that progressively change the person's relationship to the environment.
spike-jonze.framing: Keep performer and transformation in the same readable space when possible. Include a physical contact or resistance that helps an impossible effect feel tactile.
spike-jonze.rhythm: Build ordinary routine → small discovery → expanding freedom → emotional landing. Let some actions finish; cut when a new possibility opens rather than after every beat.
spike-jonze.sound: Treat the music as something the body responds to. Establish everyday room sound first, then test where the track overtakes that environment and where it recedes.
spike-jonze.typography: Keep explanatory text outside the transformation unless it has a necessary narrative role. Design any end identity to preserve the emotional landing.
spike-jonze.exceptions: Keep sincerity and physical causality as priorities. Relax automatic bans on fantasy settings, voiceover or rapid techniques; their fit depends on the specific premise.
spike-jonze.evaluation: Make a 20-second action in which one movement visibly changes the room. The viewer should name the emotional change without a caption explaining it.
spike-jonze.failureMode: Random surreal inserts interrupt the performance instead of expressing it.

evidence.summary: The Welcome Home BTS record and reporting describe a practical expanding environment built around performance. The useful lesson is the interaction of body, music and space; the evidence here is production documentation, not a new frame-by-frame measurement.

sources.title: Making Welcome Home
sources.supports: Production reference; landing page has no full transcript.

sources.title: Behind-the-Scenes Video Details Making of Spike Jonze's HomePod Ad
sources.supports: Practical expanding set and performance-led execution; evidence is reported, not a new shot analysis.

jonathan-glazer.name: Jonathan Glazer
jonathan-glazer.reference: Concept-driven advertising; Surfer provides the best documented production mechanism here.
jonathan-glazer.mechanism: One precise visual analogy becomes a forceful sensory event.
jonathan-glazer.prerequisites: Compatible plates or footage whose motion, perspective and texture can support one visual analogy.
jonathan-glazer.selection: Identify a physical correspondence first: force, direction, rhythm or shape. Select both sides of the analogy for that correspondence before choosing the most impressive shots.
jonathan-glazer.framing: Match horizon, scale, light and movement where the images must merge. Where compositing is impossible, make the relationship legible through juxtaposition rather than an unconvincing effect.
jonathan-glazer.rhythm: Give anticipation its own duration, then let the central event accumulate power. Repeat an image only when it changes scale, proximity or expectation.
jonathan-glazer.sound: Try a recognizable rhythmic figure against strongly physical effects. Leave space around the principal event so the sound is not a continuous wall of impact.
jonathan-glazer.typography: Keep the conceptual payoff visually uncluttered. End text should complete the communication rather than explain an analogy the images failed to establish.
jonathan-glazer.exceptions: No evidence supports career-wide bans on color, dialogue or off-beat cuts. Specify the selected campaign's image and sound relationship instead.
jonathan-glazer.evaluation: Create a 20-second visual analogy from two compatible movements. A viewer should describe the shared physical quality before seeing the final title.
jonathan-glazer.failureMode: Unrelated uncanny images create novelty but do not develop a concept.

evidence.summary: The Surfer collaborators describe planning and combining horse and water elements, alongside iterative post-production and sound work. Its effects depended on captured physical material and a coherent concept, not on adding an arbitrary surreal layer.

sources.title: Guinness Surfer: an oral history of the VFX
sources.supports: Horses and water plates, compositing, production planning and sound collaboration.

hal-riney.name: Hal Riney
hal-riney.reference: Restrained voice-led advertising; the 1984 Bear execution is a counterexample to an exclusively warm style.
hal-riney.mechanism: A simple spoken idea gains force from a carefully chosen everyday or symbolic image.
hal-riney.prerequisites: One intelligible proposition, specific images that can sustain it and an unforced spoken performance.
hal-riney.selection: Choose a small set of concrete actions or images with an understandable relationship to the premise. Test the concept with neutral subjects before applying any historical campaign analogy.
hal-riney.framing: Use stable compositions that allow the image to be read while the voice remains conversational. Avoid covering every noun with a separate illustrative shot.
hal-riney.rhythm: Let the proposition develop over a few connected images. Place the final sentence after the visual idea has become comprehensible, without an unnecessary extra montage.
hal-riney.sound: Record a close, natural voice with audible phrasing. Test a sparse musical or environmental motif appropriate to the concept; restrained delivery can coexist with tension.
hal-riney.typography: Use a clear final statement or identity with adequate reading time. Set a word budget from the actual sentence and frame, not an inherited maximum.
hal-riney.exceptions: Remove blanket bans on dark tone, rhythmic sound, hard cuts and statistics. Keep simplicity, vocal credibility and a coherent image-to-claim relationship.
hal-riney.evaluation: Cut a 20-second nonpolitical public-service concept. A viewer should repeat its single proposition and identify which image made it memorable.
hal-riney.failureMode: A gentle voice and nostalgic stock footage can conceal the absence of a specific idea.

evidence.summary: The museum archive's Bear advertisement combines restrained delivery with ominous imagery and sound. It shows why a Riney profile cannot be defined solely by reassurance, warmth or the absence of suspense.

sources.title: Bear
sources.author_publisher: Museum of the Moving Image, The Living Room Candidate
sources.supports: Ominous imagery and sound alongside restrained voice; one campaign execution.

michel-gondry.name: Michel Gondry
michel-gondry.reference: Inventive music-image systems; distinguish strict early correspondence from later, looser approaches.
michel-gondry.mechanism: A simple visual rule produces accumulating surprise.
michel-gondry.prerequisites: A track with distinguishable parts and repeatable actions, objects or compositing elements.
michel-gondry.selection: Choose two or three musical layers and assign each a visible behavior. Gather enough variations for the rule to evolve rather than merely repeat.
michel-gondry.framing: Make the mechanism inspectable: consistent orientation, clear silhouettes and visible spatial relationships. Allow handmade texture when it helps the viewer understand how the effect works.
michel-gondry.rhythm: Let actions within a held shot carry synchronization. Introduce a rule, repeat it clearly, then combine or violate it; compare strict mapping with a more emotional passage.
michel-gondry.sound: Work from the track's structure and separate stems where available. Map movement to timbre, entrances or phrase changes, not just kick-drum hits.
michel-gondry.typography: If type participates, give it a physical or musical behavior governed by the same system. Otherwise keep it secondary to the visual mechanism.
michel-gondry.exceptions: Replace mandatory on-grid cuts and bans on dissolves or narrative with a declared mapping rule plus permission to depart from it.
michel-gondry.evaluation: Build a 16-second study with two musical layers and two visible actions. A viewer should predict a recurrence and notice the deliberate variation.
michel-gondry.failureMode: Random stop-motion and quirky props have surface resemblance without an organizing invention.

evidence.summary: Gondry says he initially pursued precise correspondences between music and image, then moved beyond that restriction. His own account argues against enforcing every cut on the beat as a permanent signature.

sources.title: Michel Gondry Interview
sources.supports: Early precise image/music correspondence and explicit later departure from that rule.

hype-williams.name: Hype Williams
hype-williams.reference: Artist-specific music-video image-making; use a named video or period rather than a universal 1990s preset.
hype-williams.mechanism: The performer becomes an unmistakable visual icon matched to the music.
hype-williams.prerequisites: Strong performance, controlled wardrobe and set silhouettes, and coverage that preserves musical attitude.
hype-williams.selection: Start with the performer's most specific gesture or stance. Design a few contrasting setups around that identity; avoid replacing personality with generic luxury imagery.
hype-williams.framing: Test lens proximity, low viewpoint and exaggerated foreground deliberately. Check faces and body proportions rather than applying distortion indiscriminately; create readable silhouette against the set.
hype-williams.rhythm: Organize performance setups by verse, hook or musical change. Return to a signature image with increased scale or intensity; let a powerful performance hold when it carries the phrase.
hype-williams.sound: Preserve the track's authority. Use editorial accents sparingly around musical entrances; avoid stacking generic impacts over every strong beat.
hype-williams.typography: Derive supporting graphics from the artist's visual world. Letterboxing and display type are campaign choices, not mandatory proof of the style.
hype-williams.exceptions: Remove restrictions to mansions or tarmacs, compulsory distortion and bans on simplicity or narrative. Make artist identity and musical response the first selection criteria.
hype-williams.evaluation: Create a 20-second hook study using three setups. A viewer should remember one distinctive performer-image pairing without relying on the song title.
hype-williams.failureMode: Fisheye and neon applied to weak performance produce decoration rather than presence.

evidence.summary: Williams's RBMA conversation emphasizes responding to the music and seeing each artist distinctly. He also describes his changing practice, making a fixed package of fisheye, luxury locations and saturated color an inadequate career-wide rule.

sources.title: Hype Williams lecture
sources.author_publisher: Red Bull Music Academy; interview by Jeff Mao
sources.supports: Music as starting point; artist-specific visual invention and changing practice.

anton-corbijn.name: Anton Corbijn
anton-corbijn.reference: Symbolic musician portraiture; keep the music-video practice distinct from Control's historical reconstruction.
anton-corbijn.mechanism: A performer, a landscape and a recurring emblem imply an inner condition.
anton-corbijn.prerequisites: Expressive portraits, a consistent symbolic object or costume and locations that can sustain the concept.
anton-corbijn.selection: Choose an emblem that changes the performer's apparent status or isolation. Favor images with a clear bodily attitude rather than generic moody scenery.
anton-corbijn.framing: Use negative space, distance and scale to relate the person to the environment. Decide color treatment from the reference and material; preserve texture without obscuring expression.
anton-corbijn.rhythm: Alternate portrait and journey or ritual. Return to the emblem with a changed setting or relationship, allowing the repeated image to gather meaning.
anton-corbijn.sound: Let musical phrasing govern the recurrence of the motif. Test fewer cuts through a strong phrase; avoid explaining every lyric with a literal image.
anton-corbijn.typography: Treat titles and symbols as a small related visual family. A restrained handwritten or photographic treatment is an option to test, not an attributed universal rule.
anton-corbijn.exceptions: Remove the assumption that saturated color, movement or performance footage is inherently incompatible. Specify whether the target is a particular music video or Control.
anton-corbijn.evaluation: Build a 25-second sequence around one person and one object. Viewers should infer a consistent emotional relationship without being given a plot summary.
anton-corbijn.failureMode: Desaturation and grain alone cannot create a symbolic relationship.

evidence.summary: Corbijn explains that Control's monochrome relates to his memory of Joy Division and its contemporary visual culture, while explicitly noting that he also works in color. His podcast account describes Enjoy the Silence through a simple king-and-chair concept.

sources.title: Control: Anton Corbijn Interview
sources.evidence_type: First-person interview; original publication date unspecified
sources.supports: Casting for lived presence; black-and-white chosen for Joy Division's remembered visual culture.

sources.title: Ep 123: Anton Corbijn
sources.author_publisher: Midnight Chats; transcript hosted by Metacast
sources.supports: Enjoy the Silence's king and chair concept; transcript contains transcription errors.

chris-cunningham.name: Chris Cunningham
chris-cunningham.reference: Music-dependent bodily and mechanical transformation; Rubber Johnny is a specific reference.
chris-cunningham.mechanism: An apparently physical body behaves according to an unfamiliar musical logic.
chris-cunningham.prerequisites: Precisely controllable movement, convincing bodily or mechanical detail and a suitable musical structure.
chris-cunningham.selection: Gather a recognizable baseline movement before its distortion. Choose joints, contact points and materials that make the transformation readable instead of relying on vague grotesque imagery.
chris-cunningham.framing: Keep an anatomical or mechanical anchor visible through the effect. Choose clinical, nocturnal or other lighting from the specific reference, with enough detail to judge the illusion.
chris-cunningham.rhythm: Test a repeated movement first at natural timing, then against a changed musical subdivision. Escalate the rule's consequences; include a sustained moment where viewers can inspect what changed.
chris-cunningham.sound: Choose music whose texture supports the intended bodily response. Coordinate transient detail with motion, but reserve some continuous sound to prevent every edit feeling identical.
chris-cunningham.typography: Avoid explanatory typography during a perceptual reveal. Use a restrained identifying frame only where the piece needs one.
chris-cunningham.exceptions: Replace mandatory daylight, fixed discomfort holds and universal horror cues with a stated sensory premise. Effects require a baseline against which the disturbance can be perceived.
chris-cunningham.evaluation: Make a 16-second normal-to-transformed movement study. Viewers should identify both the original motion and the new rule governing it.
chris-cunningham.failureMode: Glitch overlays and fast cuts conceal rather than produce an uncanny physical idea.

evidence.summary: Cunningham describes his visual tone as dependent on the music and discusses Rubber Johnny's prolonged editing. The film's night-vision imagery directly challenges the harness's daylight-only rule. His stated interest in ambient music also complicates an exclusively aggressive stereotype.

sources.title: Interview: Chris Cunningham
sources.supports: Rubber Johnny's night vision, extended editing and music-dependent tone.

wes-anderson.name: Wes Anderson
wes-anderson.reference: Precisely staged ensemble filmmaking; The French Dispatch and Asteroid City provide collaborator evidence.
wes-anderson.mechanism: Composition and performance timing turn social relationships into visible arrangements.
wes-anderson.prerequisites: Coordinated blocking, art direction, costume and camera placement; arbitrary archive rarely supplies the required relationships.
wes-anderson.selection: Find or shoot an ensemble arrangement with a clear hierarchy and a small disruption. Choose a gesture or entrance whose position in the frame carries the joke.
wes-anderson.framing: Plan lateral and depth relationships before centering the camera. Use readable planes and deliberate eyelines; symmetry should organize behavior rather than crop away essential context.
wes-anderson.rhythm: Hold the arrangement long enough to register, then time an entrance, reveal or cut to its change. Alternate tableau and detail when the detail revises the social situation.
wes-anderson.sound: Keep dialogue timing and small practical sounds precise. Try a musical passage with a defined entrance or exit, rather than continuously signaling whimsy.
wes-anderson.typography: Design chapter and title typography as part of the chosen fictional publication, institution or era. A fixed font and pastel palette cannot replace that design logic.
wes-anderson.exceptions: Remove bans on natural light, spatial depth and off-center staging. Require a reason for composition and a readable performance beat.
wes-anderson.evaluation: Shoot a 20-second three-person tableau with one entrance or rearrangement. The viewer should understand the status change before dialogue explains it.
wes-anderson.failureMode: Centered stock shots with a pastel grade imitate packaging while missing the staging.

evidence.summary: Robert Yeoman describes animatic-led blocking and lens choices that keep ensemble positions readable. The ASC's Asteroid City interview synopsis explicitly documents extensive natural and practical lighting, contradicting a blanket artificial-light assumption.

sources.title: Robert Yeoman, ASC, on Shooting Wes Anderson's The French Dispatch

christopher-nolan.name: Christopher Nolan
christopher-nolan.reference: Braided time and escalating dramatic information; Oppenheimer is the principal editing reference.
christopher-nolan.mechanism: Separate strands acquire urgency as their relationship becomes intelligible.
christopher-nolan.prerequisites: Distinct causal strands, reliable chronology and identifiable characters or processes.
christopher-nolan.selection: Assign every candidate shot to a strand and a specific change of state. Choose correspondences with narrative significance, not just matching motion.
christopher-nolan.framing: Give strands stable orientation or visual distinctions. Preserve enough context for a face, object or place to be recognized when it returns.
christopher-nolan.rhythm: Establish each strand before accelerating alternation. Shorten intervals only as the relationship becomes clearer; let a sustained performance interrupt the mechanism when it adds weight.
christopher-nolan.sound: Try one repeating pulse or motif whose orchestration changes with convergence. Use an intentional dropout or acoustic shift to make a decisive moment legible.
christopher-nolan.typography: Use dates or locations where viewers need them. Typography may disambiguate time; it should not be asked to repair a fundamentally unreadable braid.
christopher-nolan.exceptions: Keep strand progression and causal clarity. Relax universal bans on songs, dissolves, humor and slow motion; preserve the reference's dramatic function rather than an effects blacklist.
christopher-nolan.evaluation: Create a 30-second two-strand sequence ending in a shared consequence. Ask viewers to explain the relationship and temporal order before increasing the cut rate.
christopher-nolan.failureMode: A ticking clock over alternating archive suggests urgency without establishing causality.

evidence.summary: Jennifer Lame discusses controlling the information load in Oppenheimer and preserving performance within its complex structure. Ludwig Goransson's account describes substantial music development before editing, reinforcing the connection between score and dramatic character.

sources.title: Jennifer Lame interview | How to edit Oppenheimer (and win a BAFTA while you do it)
sources.supports: Controlling information load and anchoring complex structure in performance.

sources.title: Oppenheimer composer Ludwig Goransson interview

denis-villeneuve.name: Denis Villeneuve
denis-villeneuve.reference: Sensory scale and character tension; Joe Walker's account of Dune is the concrete reference.
denis-villeneuve.mechanism: A small human perception or gesture gains force against a vast environment.
denis-villeneuve.prerequisites: Coherent environment coverage plus meaningful human detail; scale alone is insufficient.
denis-villeneuve.selection: Pair a spatially imposing image with a precise bodily response, gesture or practical task. Reject interchangeable landscapes that do not change the character's situation.
denis-villeneuve.framing: Make scale readable through a person, doorway or movement. Preserve negative space when it creates anticipation; move closer when a small action becomes decisive.
denis-villeneuve.rhythm: Try environment → detail → altered perception. Compare a patient approach with a sharp sensory transition; keep the version that communicates the actual change of state.
denis-villeneuve.sound: Establish an acoustic world with a recognizable texture, then change it deliberately at the transition. Give an intimate gesture enough sonic room to register.
denis-villeneuve.typography: Use sparse contextual text when necessary. Decide title scale and spacing from the fictional world; minimal typography is an option, not a substitute for narrative orientation.
denis-villeneuve.exceptions: Remove automatic prohibitions on fast cuts, flares, melody and reactions. Specify whether a shot carries scale, apprehension, intimacy or transition.
denis-villeneuve.evaluation: Build a 25-second sequence in which a small gesture changes the meaning of a large image. Viewers should remember the gesture as well as the spectacle.
denis-villeneuve.failureMode: Huge wides, orange fog and a low drone can remain emotionally empty.

evidence.summary: Walker describes deliberate flares, matched sensory transitions, an abrupt change of environment and an intimate touch held for its emotional effect. This is a more varied practice than the harness's bans on flares, sharp transitions and expressive reactions suggest.

sources.title: Dune Editor Joe Walker on Cutting Denis Villeneuve's Sweeping Epic
sources.author_publisher: Hugh Hart, Motion Picture Association / The Credits
sources.supports: Sensory transitions, deliberate flares and intimate gesture within epic scale.

edgar-wright.name: Edgar Wright
edgar-wright.reference: Designed audiovisual comedy and musical action; music-video and feature practice should inform the edit together.
edgar-wright.mechanism: Setup, action, sound and payoff form a pattern the audience can recognize and anticipate.
edgar-wright.prerequisites: Setup and payoff coverage, specific action sounds, readable motion and performances whose timing can carry the joke.
edgar-wright.selection: Choose actions with a beginning, contact and consequence. Build a bank of matched mundane details that can recur with changed meaning; prioritize actual visual jokes over unrelated energetic shots.
edgar-wright.framing: Keep the geography of an action clear before compressing it. Compose entrances, exits and background information so the frame can deliver a reveal without an explanatory cut.
edgar-wright.rhythm: Try a short patterned burst, a deliberate pause and a payoff. Repeat an established action with one changed element; test some beats inside a held shot.
edgar-wright.sound: Map selected actions to the music, preserving dialogue punchlines and physical contacts. Alternate close, dry practical sounds with broader musical passages to create contrast.
edgar-wright.typography: Animate type when it participates in a specific joke or rhythmic event. Distinguish the film title from supporting cards and let both have an intentional entrance and exit.
edgar-wright.exceptions: Replace every-cut synchronization, all-diegetic-music and no-natural-pause rules with a required audiovisual setup/payoff relationship. Timing should serve anticipation and surprise.
edgar-wright.evaluation: Make a 20-second three-action setup followed by a changed repetition. Viewers should recognize the pattern and describe the variation as the payoff.
edgar-wright.failureMode: Whip transitions and impact sounds cannot manufacture a joke absent from the footage.

evidence.summary: Wright's RBMA conversation describes music planning and the After Hours long-take video as preparation for work in Shaun of the Dead. Musical construction can therefore happen within a continuous shot; it is not synonymous with cutting on every transient.

sources.title: Edgar Wright lecture
sources.author_publisher: Red Bull Music Academy; conversation with Brian Reitzell
sources.supports: Music planning and the After Hours long-take music video as preparation for Shaun of the Dead.

terrence-malick.name: Terrence Malick
terrence-malick.reference: Associative memory and embodied perception; The Tree of Life and Mark Yoshikawa's editing account.
terrence-malick.mechanism: Image, gesture and voice suggest an experience larger than any literal illustration.
terrence-malick.prerequisites: Intimate gestures, environmental interaction and sustained observational coverage with a consistent sensory world.
terrence-malick.selection: Collect physical experiences tied to a subject: touch, balance, breath, movement through a room or landscape. Avoid stock hands-and-sunlight imagery disconnected from a person or memory.
terrence-malick.framing: Stay responsive to an action's changing direction and available light. Preserve proximity and environmental relation; a floating camera should follow perception rather than wander without purpose.
terrence-malick.rhythm: Try an image sequence first, then add a short reflective voice passage whose meaning extends it. Remove overly literal matches and compare complete gestures with selected fragments.
terrence-malick.sound: Let voice, environment and music carry different aspects of the memory. Leave an unscored passage or a breath of room sound where it makes the experience more concrete.
terrence-malick.typography: Use minimal orientation outside the associative passage. A date or place can locate a memory without interpreting its emotional meaning.
terrence-malick.exceptions: Replace absolute bans on tripod, artificial light, night interiors and completed actions with preferences tied to the selected film. Preserve intentionality beneath apparent spontaneity.
terrence-malick.evaluation: Make a 25-second memory passage. The voice should add a thought the images cannot state alone, while the images contribute something absent from the words.
terrence-malick.failureMode: Backlit fragments plus philosophical narration can feel arbitrary when they lack a specific remembered experience.

evidence.summary: Lubezki describes responsive available-light work with practical exceptions. Yoshikawa explains a deliberately shaped associative edit and warns against voiceover becoming too literally illustrated by the picture.

sources.title: Emmanuel Lubezki AMC ASC: The Tree of Life
sources.supports: Available light, responsive shooting and exceptions to lighting practice.

sources.title: Mark Yoshikawa Talks of Editing Terrence Malick, Christopher Guest, and the New Reminiscence
sources.supports: Malick voice/image disjunction; Guest footage review and comic timing. Shared source across two profiles.

frank-capra.name: Frank Capra
frank-capra.reference: The Why We Fight compilation documentaries, not Capra's entire dramatic and comic career.
frank-capra.mechanism: A clearly stated argument is developed through organized archival evidence and explanation.
frank-capra.prerequisites: Provenanced footage, a defensible explanatory proposition and maps or diagrams where geography matters.
frank-capra.selection: Arrange material as proposition, evidence and consequence. Keep the origin of appropriated footage visible in the research record and avoid presenting an opponent's staged imagery as neutral observation.
frank-capra.framing: Preserve the action or institution needed for the argument. Use a map at the scale required to explain movement, with labels that can be read at normal playback.
frank-capra.rhythm: Let each section answer a distinct question. Alternate an assertion with an example or explanation; use comparison where it adds a verifiable relationship.
frank-capra.sound: Record narration with clear sentence structure and emphasis. Test music by whether it clarifies the section's dramatic role, without letting certainty of tone replace evidence.
frank-capra.typography: Use maps, dates and source labels to make the argument inspectable. Distinguish historical propaganda graphics from newly authored explanatory material.
frank-capra.exceptions: Rename or scope the profile to Why We Fight. Remove career-wide claims about neutrality, contemporary music or graphics; preserve archival attribution and argumentative clarity.
frank-capra.evaluation: Create a 30-second historical explanation with one claim, two source-backed examples and one map. Viewers should separate the factual evidence from the narrator's interpretation.
frank-capra.failureMode: Authoritative narration and marching music can give an unsupported compilation the appearance of proof.

evidence.summary: The National Archives account describes Prelude to War's compilation of existing material, narration and explanatory animation. These are historically situated propaganda films; their confident form does not make every historical claim independently reliable.

sources.title: Why We Fight: Prelude to War, America's Crash History Lesson
sources.author_publisher: US National Archives, The Unwritten Record
sources.supports: Compilation propaganda, narration and animated explanatory material.

sergei-eisenstein.name: Sergei Eisenstein
sergei-eisenstein.reference: Expressive montage and staging; distinguish silent-film montage from the later sound films.
sergei-eisenstein.mechanism: Relationships between images and bodily forms create an idea or conflict.
sergei-eisenstein.prerequisites: Images with a purposeful conceptual or graphic relation; for staged work, precise poses and movement.
sergei-eisenstein.selection: Write the intended relationship between two images before selecting them. Choose contrast in scale, direction, social role or gesture that adds a thought beyond either image alone.
sergei-eisenstein.framing: Treat bodies, architecture and shadows as active compositional forms. A held arrangement may express a conflict more clearly than additional cutting.
sergei-eisenstein.rhythm: Test the same material in two orders. Use repetition, duration and collision to develop an argument; speed up only when the increasing pressure remains intelligible.
sergei-eisenstein.sound: For a sound-film reference, plan music and gesture together or test deliberate audiovisual counterpoint. Do not force all material into a modern beat grid.
sergei-eisenstein.typography: Intertitles can state or complicate a proposition, but should not merely explain every juxtaposition. Choose color from the specific reference rather than a historical stereotype.
sergei-eisenstein.exceptions: Remove universal bans on color, camera movement, individual psychology and continuity. Preserve deliberate relations between shots and expressive staging.
sergei-eisenstein.evaluation: Build two 20-second sequences from the same six images in different orders. Viewers should identify a meaning changed by the arrangement, not only a different pace.
sergei-eisenstein.failureMode: Fast cutting between unrelated images creates density without a dialectical or dramatic relationship.

evidence.summary: Criterion's analysis of Ivan the Terrible documents expressive performance, musical construction and a color sequence. Bordwell's account foregrounds staging derived from dance and painting. These counter the harness's reduction to silent, monochrome, impersonal rapid montage.

sources.title: Ivan the Terrible, Parts I and II
sources.supports: Performance, color, music and expressive staging beyond a silent-montage stereotype.

sources.title: Staging and Performance in Ivan the Terrible, Part 2
sources.evidence_type: Film scholar's original audiovisual analysis; publisher synopsis
sources.supports: Expressive movement and the relationship to painting and dance.

tony-schwartz.name: Tony Schwartz
tony-schwartz.reference: Sound-centered advertising; Daisy is a historical case with DDB collaborators, not a universal solo-authored template.
tony-schwartz.mechanism: A familiar sound changes meaning through a sharply designed association.
tony-schwartz.prerequisites: A recognizable sound pattern, a contrasting second pattern and a concept that can be understood without misleading context.
tony-schwartz.selection: For a neutral demonstration, find two sounds that share a structure but imply different situations. Choose a simple visual action capable of holding attention through the transition.
tony-schwartz.framing: Keep attention on the sound's source until the change needs a different image. A closer framing should have a perceptual purpose rather than serve as generic tension.
tony-schwartz.rhythm: Design the sound transition first, then place the visual change where it alters interpretation. Avoid extra inserts that compete with the central association.
tony-schwartz.sound: Shape the handoff in rhythm, perspective and loudness. Test whether the listener can identify both sources; retain clarity rather than relying on a startling peak.
tony-schwartz.typography: Use a concise identifying or explanatory end frame when needed. Do not assume all necessary context must fit into the sound association itself.
tony-schwartz.exceptions: Replace one-ad prohibitions with a sound-first concept requirement. Credit the agency and collaborators, and separate historical persuasion analysis from factual validation.
tony-schwartz.evaluation: Create a 15-second nonpolitical sound study, such as a domestic timer becoming a race-start cue. A listener should identify the shift before reading the end frame.
tony-schwartz.failureMode: An abrupt loud sound is a startle; it becomes an idea only when the association is meaningful.

evidence.summary: The archived Daisy transcript shows a child's counting yielding to a countdown and explosion, followed by political voiceover. The specific transition matters more than a general rule forbidding music, montage or additional voices.

sources.title: Peace Little Girl (Daisy)
sources.author_publisher: Museum of the Moving Image, The Living Room Candidate
sources.evidence_type: Primary advertisement transcript and institutional attribution

lincoln-project.name: The Lincoln Project
lincoln-project.reference: An organization and its campaign teams; Ben Howe's 2020 interview is the bounded reference.
lincoln-project.mechanism: Existing statements are organized to make a contradiction or consequence easy to follow.
lincoln-project.prerequisites: Verifiable statements with their full context, dates and relevant documented outcomes.
lincoln-project.selection: Build a statement ledger before a selects reel. Pair claims only where the relationship is fair and the chronology is clear; preserve qualifications that change the proposition.
lincoln-project.framing: Use recognizable source framing and leave room for unobtrusive provenance. Avoid crops that imply a reaction to an event occurring elsewhere or later.
lincoln-project.rhythm: Test assertion → relevant evidence → concise consequence. Let the actual statement remain intelligible; additional montage should contribute a new fact rather than merely intensify tone.
lincoln-project.sound: Keep source dialogue intelligible and distinguish editorial effects from recorded sound. Test a restrained and an unscored version before committing to an emotional bed.
lincoln-project.typography: Label quotation, date and source consistently. A graphic may summarize an established contrast; it should not introduce a stronger unsupported allegation.
lincoln-project.exceptions: Replace organizational style absolutes with a campaign-specific brief. Keep factual context as a firm requirement and treat ominous music, attack tone and typography as choices.
lincoln-project.evaluation: Use a nonpolitical institutional claim and documented result in a 20-second evidence comparison. Viewers should identify the contradiction and the source of both halves.
lincoln-project.failureMode: A forceful montage can mislead if it erases the dates or qualifications that make the comparison fair.

evidence.summary: Howe describes constructing scripts from existing quotations so the material carries the story. This supports a source-led assembly practice, but does not establish one permanent visual, musical or tonal style for the organization.

sources.title: Meet the Lincoln Project's Video Wiz, Who's Driving Trump Insane
sources.supports: Writing through selection and assembly of existing quotations; campaign-specific evidence.

mark-woollen.name: Mark Woollen
mark-woollen.reference: Concept-led feature-film trailers; The Social Network campaign is a documented reference.
mark-woollen.mechanism: A distinctive music-and-image proposition sells the film's emotional experience.
mark-woollen.prerequisites: Strong character moments, a film-specific premise and an editable musical cue whose structure supports the concept.
mark-woollen.selection: Create separate reels for emotional promise, premise clarity and memorable images. Choose one organizing tension before assembling chronology; keep enough setup for strangers to understand the stakes.
mark-woollen.framing: Preserve the intended subject and useful negative space when adapting source shots. Select footage whose visual relationships survive trailer compression.
mark-woollen.rhythm: Try hook → emotional proposition → complication → escalating promise → unresolved final image. Rearrange for the trailer's argument while avoiding false story claims.
mark-woollen.sound: Audition substantially different musical interpretations of the same selects. Plan a recognizable opening, space for dialogue, a change of musical state and a final punctuation; the cue need not be a cover or choir.
mark-woollen.typography: Write cards as part of the concept. Give the film title a distinct typographic event and check that reviews or credentials do not interrupt the emotional progression.
mark-woollen.exceptions: Remove categorical bans on narration, risers, rapid montage and premise explanation. Require a named campaign reference and a concept-led music rationale.
mark-woollen.evaluation: Make two 30-second concepts from the same footage with different music structures. Ask viewers what film experience each promises, not merely which is louder.
mark-woollen.failureMode: An unusual song over beautiful clips may feel tasteful while failing to sell a specific movie.

evidence.summary: Woollen's WIRED interview describes music selection, developing alternative concepts and obtaining extra material for The Social Network. These are creative development choices, not evidence for a permanent ban on voiceover, fast montage or plot information.

sources.title: Secrets of a Trailer Guru: How This Guy Gets You to the Movies
sources.author_publisher: Jason Kehe, WIRED; Mark Woollen interview
sources.supports: Music casting, multiple concepts and additional material for The Social Network campaign.

sources.title: Mark Woollen and Michael Greenfeld
sources.supports: Trailer construction; two speakers must not be conflated.

buddha-jones.name: Buddha Jones
buddha-jones.reference: A trailer agency with multiple teams and campaigns; use Bill Neil's craft discussion and credited examples, not a single horror formula.
buddha-jones.mechanism: Controlled information and changing sonic pressure build anticipation and reversal.
buddha-jones.prerequisites: A legible hook, escalating source events, a strong reveal or reversal and independently editable dialogue, music and effects.
buddha-jones.selection: Rank clips by what they disclose: rule, threat, reaction, escalation or payoff. Choose one distinctive set piece for identity and enough connective material to make its stakes readable.
buddha-jones.framing: Protect spatial orientation before a surprise. Select approach and reaction coverage that can sustain expectation without relying entirely on black frames.
buddha-jones.rhythm: Try a complete miniature scene as the opening, then a change of scale and a compressed final passage. Reserve a reversal or button for after the audience thinks the section has ended.
buddha-jones.sound: Build separate tracks for atmosphere, pulse, transitions, impacts and dialogue. Design contrast in density and silence; derive a recurring motif from the film when the source supports it.
buddha-jones.typography: Give cards, title and end information distinct jobs. Synchronize a title entrance to a chosen event rather than adding a hit to every text appearance.
buddha-jones.exceptions: Replace universal horror rules with campaign-specific reveal strategy. Allow finished actions, warmth, narration and non-black transitions where they strengthen the promise.
buddha-jones.evaluation: Build a 30-second trailer passage with one deliberate pressure release and reversal. Viewers should anticipate one event and clearly register the changed expectation.
buddha-jones.failureMode: Continuous risers and black-frame impacts exhaust contrast before the important reveal.

evidence.summary: Vox's Bill Neil interview description explicitly identifies sound design and rug pulls as trailer techniques. The Clio record supplies a specific Buddha Jones campaign reference for Boots. Neither source establishes that every agency trailer must cut to black or hide every reveal.
evidence.basis: Primary interview synopsis and campaign credit; detailed timing remains to be measured

sources.title: Iconic movie trailers, explained by a trailer editor
sources.supports: Trailer editor's sound design and reversal techniques; full transcript not available here.

sources.title: 28 Years Later: Boots
sources.supports: Specific trailer credit and campaign reference; not an agency-wide formula.

a24.name: A24
a24.reference: A studio and distributor; define the actual film campaign and credited agency before prescribing craft.
a24.mechanism: Campaign specificity is the useful starting point; there is no defensible single-director system.
a24.prerequisites: One named trailer version with credits, its film-specific hook and footage that supports that promise.
a24.selection: Write the campaign's promise in one sentence, then select a distinctive character, object or situation that can carry it. Separate an intriguing omission from missing basic premise information.
a24.framing: Choose a consistent image logic from the film itself: intimacy, geometry, texture or scale. Do not apply a studio-wide palette to incompatible source footage.
a24.rhythm: Develop one concrete reference version. Test how much orientation viewers need before ambiguity becomes productive; let pace follow the campaign rather than an assumed 'art-house' duration.
a24.sound: Choose a sonic identity grounded in that film's material or campaign concept. Record which cue, motif and silence pattern belong to the reference instead of calling them A24 defaults.
a24.typography: Research the specific campaign's title and supporting cards. Allow premise lines, reviews and multiple typographic roles when they have a clear purpose.
a24.exceptions: Reclassify as a campaign collection or studio filter. Remove blanket bans on voiceover, explanations, montage and card counts; attach actual agency and version metadata.
a24.evaluation: Make a 20-second concept whose film-specific promise remains clear after hiding the studio logo. If the only identifiable attribute is the logo, the profile is not specific enough.
a24.failureMode: Sparse cards and eerie music can imitate a marketing stereotype without capturing any particular campaign.

It provides a concrete attribution correction, not proof of a universal A24 editing formula.
evidence.basis: Primary campaign credit; broader style claim unsupported

tony-zhou.name: Taylor Ramos & Tony Zhou
tony-zhou.reference: Every Frame a Painting by Taylor Ramos and Tony Zhou; the 2017 retrospective describes a particular period.
tony-zhou.mechanism: The viewer sees an argument demonstrated through the audiovisual evidence itself.
tony-zhou.prerequisites: Clips that directly demonstrate a formal claim, with source identification and enough surrounding action to understand the comparison.
tony-zhou.selection: Find the demonstration before polishing the narration. Choose contrasting examples that isolate the same decision: staging, framing, movement, sound or cut timing.
tony-zhou.framing: Preserve the original composition when the claim depends on it. Use a crop, freeze or annotation only to direct attention to the specific evidence under discussion.
tony-zhou.rhythm: Try uninterrupted example → concise explanation → replay or comparison. Give the viewer a chance to perceive the difference; avoid talking across the exact sound or action being analyzed.
tony-zhou.sound: Switch deliberately between original clip sound and explanatory voice. If the claim concerns music or effects, replay that passage without a competing bed.
tony-zhou.typography: Credit the film and relevant makers. Keep arrows, labels and split screens functional; typography should point to evidence rather than replace it.
tony-zhou.exceptions: Correct the profile's visible credit to include Taylor Ramos. Keep evidence-first demonstration and source labels, while allowing new footage or other formats when the argument needs them.
tony-zhou.evaluation: Make a 30-second essay on one editing choice. Afterward, viewers should locate that choice in a new clip rather than merely repeat the narrator's terminology.
tony-zhou.failureMode: An articulate voiceover over film clips can remain an illustrated opinion with no actual demonstration.

evidence.summary: Ramos and Zhou explicitly correct the series' coauthorship and describe explaining visual ideas by showing them. Their retrospective also recognizes that their chosen format could become constraining, which argues against treating its original limits as permanent laws.

sources.title: Postmortem
sources.author_publisher: Taylor Ramos and Tony Zhou, Every Frame a Painting / Medium
sources.supports: Coauthorship, visual demonstration, footage-led argument and limitations of their format.

johnny-harris.name: Johnny Harris
johnny-harris.reference: Visual explanatory journalism; the 2025 How I Write interview supplies workflow evidence, not universal map rules.
johnny-harris.mechanism: A question is developed through visual explanation with a clear promise to the viewer.
johnny-harris.prerequisites: An answerable question, source-backed facts and graphics whose information can be traced to those facts.
johnny-harris.selection: Build a paired script: each claim beside the visual evidence or explanation that carries it. Prefer a document, place or comparison that resolves the question over generic illustrative footage.
johnny-harris.framing: On maps, establish geography before moving to the relevant location. Keep orientation and scale visible long enough to support the claim; show the host where personal inquiry adds context.
johnny-harris.rhythm: Open a specific information gap, demonstrate the key relationship and update the question. Alternate explanation and encounter when each contributes something the other cannot.
johnny-harris.sound: Use music changes to distinguish inquiry, discovery and synthesis. Keep dense explanations acoustically simple; avoid treating every map move as an action-trailer transition.
johnny-harris.typography: Make labels and source dates readable. Animate routes, boundaries or comparisons only when movement conveys information; distinguish schematics from exact geography.
johnny-harris.exceptions: Replace no-desk, no-label and map-by-default rules with a visual justification for each claim. Flag uncertain source claims independently from presentation polish.
johnny-harris.evaluation: Build a 30-second map explanation. Viewers should state the relationship the animation demonstrated and distinguish it from a merely decorative camera move.
johnny-harris.failureMode: Moving maps and handwritten marks can create the appearance of investigation without supplying evidence.

evidence.summary: The interview publisher's notes and chapters identify visual scripting, video-first thinking and story promise. They support those workflow topics, but do not substantiate arbitrary map frequency, label bans or a prohibition on desk-based presentation.
evidence.basis: Primary interview notes; detailed visual prescriptions proposed

christopher-guest.name: Christopher Guest
christopher-guest.reference: Improvised ensemble comedy in Guest-directed films such as Best in Show; do not credit him as director of This Is Spinal Tap.
christopher-guest.mechanism: Committed characters reveal the gap between their self-image and observable behavior.
christopher-guest.prerequisites: Believable character desires, improvised or natural conversational detail and reactions from the actual exchange.
christopher-guest.selection: Choose a statement of self-belief and a behavior that complicates it. Prefer sincere specificity to performers signaling that they know they are funny.
christopher-guest.framing: Let characters share space when the relationship carries the humor. Reserve a closer reaction for a meaningful change, not a compulsory cue telling viewers to laugh.
christopher-guest.rhythm: Protect the setup and find the smallest pause that allows the contradiction to register. Compare a held reaction with an earlier cut; select by the performance's actual timing.
christopher-guest.sound: Keep conversational texture and intelligible details. Test the joke without score first; add music only when the scene's own premise or chosen reference justifies it.
christopher-guest.typography: Use ordinary documentary identification when it supports the fiction. Avoid exaggerated caption commentary that announces the joke before the character reveals it.
christopher-guest.exceptions: Keep respect for sincere performance. Remove fixed rules that every answer must remain whole or every awkward pause must be extended; the comedy is shaped in selection and timing.
christopher-guest.evaluation: Create a 25-second character introduction with one self-description and one contradicting action. Viewers should identify the character's belief before explaining the joke.
christopher-guest.failureMode: Random pauses, zooms and reaction shots can ridicule a person without creating a coherent comic character.

evidence.summary: The Best in Show production account describes outline-based improvisation and extensive editing. Mark Yoshikawa emphasizes reviewing the material and finding comic timing in performance, supporting a selective rather than mechanically uncut approach.

sources.title: Best in Show
sources.supports: Improvised material developed from an outline and shaped extensively in editing.

sources.title: Mark Yoshikawa Talks of Editing Terrence Malick, Christopher Guest, and the New Reminiscence

mrbeast.name: MrBeast
mrbeast.reference: Large-premise challenge and spectacle videos; specify a dated reference rather than assuming one enduring editing cadence.
mrbeast.mechanism: A legible objective, stakes and changing progress sustain attention.
mrbeast.prerequisites: A real objective, comprehensible rules, observable progress, consequential choices and an authentic payoff.
mrbeast.selection: Choose material that establishes what someone wants, what makes it difficult and what changes. Prefer decisions and consequences over interchangeable excited reactions.
mrbeast.framing: Make the scale and rules visible in the same shot where possible. Use close-ups to clarify effort or choice, and wide views to establish the actual challenge.
mrbeast.rhythm: Open with a clear promise and evidence that the premise exists. Introduce a real complication or secondary objective when the situation becomes repetitive. Compress repeated attempts while preserving decisions and consequences.
mrbeast.sound: Use score and effects to mark changes of state rather than every cut. Protect dialogue explaining a rule or choice, and create headroom before the largest payoff.
mrbeast.typography: Display progress when it changes or needs clarification. Counters must reflect real measurements; persistent numbers are optional if the scene already communicates the state.
mrbeast.exceptions: Remove the universal four-second cap, compulsory riser-hit reveals and permanent on-screen counters. Evaluate clarity and progression separately from cut density.
mrbeast.evaluation: Make a 30-second miniature challenge with a genuine mid-sequence complication. Viewers should state the objective and explain how the new situation changes what they expect next.
mrbeast.failureMode: Relentless cuts and escalating adjectives cannot replace real progress or a payoff.

evidence.summary: In the 2021 Colin and Samir interview, Donaldson explains that a long video often needs a secondary story or changed situation to renew interest. This is a narrative development principle, not evidence for a universal four-second shot ceiling. Later interview notes document the growing production scale.
