casey-neistat.name: Casey Neistat
casey-neistat.reference: Personal action-led filmmaking and vlogs; Make It Count is a concrete edit-discovery reference.
casey-neistat.mechanism: A personal intention becomes an improvised journey with a visible result.
casey-neistat.prerequisites: A real personal objective, action coverage, spatial context and evidence of what changed.
casey-neistat.selection: Build a day or journey around an intention and obstacle. Collect practical transitions such as leaving, traveling, arriving and doing, alongside the most revealing unexpected moment.
casey-neistat.framing: Use self-placement, wide context and tactile details to establish presence. An improvised camera position can feel purposeful when it clearly shows the action.
casey-neistat.rhythm: Try intention → attempt → complication → revised action → result. Use travel compression between meaningful scenes; retain an imperfect take if its event is stronger.
casey-neistat.sound: Let actual city, travel or task sounds establish place. Use a music phrase to compress movement, then step out of it for a decisive encounter or spoken thought.
casey-neistat.typography: Use handwritten or physical notes only when they express planning, evidence or personality. A map should explain the journey rather than function as a compulsory vlog transition.
casey-neistat.exceptions: Relax bans on studio, desk, static shots and dissolves. Keep first-person agency and a clear story of doing something.
casey-neistat.evaluation: Build a 30-second personal errand film. A viewer should identify the initial intention and what altered it, even with the music muted.
casey-neistat.failureMode: Timelapses and travel montages show activity without a personal story.

evidence.summary: Neistat's Little Black Book interview describes finding Make It Count's story from a substantial body of travel footage. It supports discovering structure through editing and treating equipment as a means, not defining the style by particular cameras or transitions.

sources.title: Breakfast with Casey Neistat
sources.supports: Finding Make It Count's story from substantial travel footage in the edit.

mkbhd.name: MKBHD
mkbhd.reference: Scripted technology explanation and review; Brownlee's own course is the principal craft reference.
mkbhd.mechanism: A clear judgment is supported by an immediately relevant demonstration.
mkbhd.prerequisites: Hands-on observations, reproducible demonstrations, useful comparisons and clean product coverage.
mkbhd.selection: Pair every major judgment with a demonstration or clearly identified observation. Separate attractive product images from shots that actually support a claim.
mkbhd.framing: Control reflections, background separation and focus so the relevant feature is visible. Choose a static view when it makes a comparison easier than a moving beauty shot.
mkbhd.rhythm: Move from judgment to evidence with minimal friction. Group related features into a coherent argument; avoid repeating specifications that do not change the viewer's understanding.
mkbhd.sound: Prioritize an even, intelligible voice. Keep music subordinate during measurements and comparisons; use product sound where it demonstrates something relevant.
mkbhd.typography: Show units, comparison conditions and a meaningful baseline. Use restrained hierarchy and adequate size; red, one typeface and a fixed animation style are optional design choices.
mkbhd.exceptions: Remove aesthetic bans on non-red colors, effects, jokes and rapid cuts. Require contextualized evidence and a purpose for the product shot.
mkbhd.evaluation: Create a 25-second feature assessment with one comparison. Viewers should recall the practical conclusion and what evidence supports it, not only the specification.
mkbhd.failureMode: Beautiful product footage can make an unsupported opinion look more rigorous than it is.

evidence.summary: Brownlee describes extensive scripting, deciding A-roll and B-roll during writing, and putting numbers in comparative context. He explicitly says sophisticated camera equipment is not necessary. This makes explanatory shot design more fundamental than a red accent or robotic move.

sources.title: YouTube Success: Script, Shoot & Edit with MKBHD
sources.supports: Research, scripting, A-roll/B-roll planning and contextualizing measurements.

tom-scott.name: Tom Scott
tom-scott.reference: Concise factual entertainment about a specific real thing; distinguish this format from Scott's other shows.
tom-scott.mechanism: A surprising proposition leads to an understandable mechanism and its limit.
tom-scott.prerequisites: A precise factual question, a location or object that helps answer it and enough evidence to explain the mechanism.
tom-scott.selection: Choose the physical detail that makes the premise surprising. Include evidence of how it works and one boundary or exception; do not rely on the location merely as an attractive background.
tom-scott.framing: Position the presenter relative to the relevant object. Cut closer or add a diagram when the mechanism cannot be seen from the establishing view.
tom-scott.rhythm: Try surprising claim → real-world demonstration → explanation → qualification. Remove detours that do not help the central question, while retaining necessary caveats.
tom-scott.sound: Make speech and relevant location sound clear. Music and additional coverage are choices to test, not categorically forbidden; avoid competing with the explanation.
tom-scott.typography: Use a label, number or diagram when it reduces verbal load. Keep scale and units clear, and avoid unsupported precision.
tom-scott.exceptions: Replace bans on cuts within takes, music and supplementary coverage with a requirement that every addition improve understanding of the specific thing.
tom-scott.evaluation: Explain one unusual piece of infrastructure in 30 seconds. A viewer should describe both what is surprising and how it works.
tom-scott.failureMode: A presenter in an interesting location can still deliver a generic fact list.

evidence.summary: In the Waveform interview, Scott describes a factual-entertainment sensibility and explains reframing an aquarium through a spaceship analogy. He also discusses different formats, undermining the idea that his entire practice is one uninterrupted on-location take.

sources.title: How Tom Scott Makes Videos
sources.author_publisher: Waveform: The MKBHD Podcast; transcript hosted by Podscripts
sources.supports: Factual-entertainment premise, format differences and aquarium/spaceship analogy.

veritasium.name: Veritasium
veritasium.reference: Misconception-aware science explanation; distinguish educational evidence from assumptions about platform engagement.
veritasium.mechanism: A plausible mental model is tested and revised through evidence.
veritasium.prerequisites: A testable proposition, a plausible misconception, a valid demonstration and an explanation of its conditions.
veritasium.selection: Find an experiment that distinguishes the competing explanations. Capture the setup, relevant variables, observation and a useful comparison; retain results that complicate the expected story.
veritasium.framing: Keep cause and effect visible together where feasible. Add close coverage or a diagram for hidden mechanisms, clearly distinguishing measurement from illustration.
veritasium.rhythm: Try prediction → test → observed mismatch → revised explanation → transfer question. Change this order if prior context is necessary; surprise should serve understanding.
veritasium.sound: Protect the actual observation and its explanation from distracting cues. Use musical change to mark a conceptual turn, not to imply that a result is more certain than it is.
veritasium.typography: Display relevant variables, units and uncertainty. Let the diagram evolve as the explanation changes; avoid illustrating an incorrect model without clearly identifying it.
veritasium.exceptions: Replace mandatory demo-first ordering and blanket cutting or music bans with a test of whether the viewer's initial model has actually changed.
veritasium.evaluation: Create a 30-second misconception demonstration, then ask viewers to predict a different example. Correct transfer is stronger evidence of learning than recalling the reveal.
veritasium.failureMode: A surprising result without a repaired mental model can leave the original misconception intact.

evidence.summary: Muller's physics-education thesis examines multimedia explanations that engage learners' alternative conceptions. Its educational context matters: it does not establish a universal YouTube story order or prove that every surprising demonstration improves retention.

vsauce.name: Vsauce
vsauce.reference: Conversational conceptual essays; Michael Stevens's 2014 AMA documents the writing and delivery process.
vsauce.mechanism: A small question opens a chain of meaningful conceptual connections.
vsauce.prerequisites: A compelling question, source-backed conceptual links and visual demonstrations for abstract transitions.
vsauce.selection: Choose examples that make the next conceptual step feel earned. For every apparent tangent, write its connection to the central question before sourcing decorative footage.
vsauce.framing: Use presenter contact for inquiry and a clear object or diagram for the key abstraction. Shift scale only when the conceptual move requires it.
vsauce.rhythm: Build question → surprising connection → deeper implication → return or reframing. Allow a direct answer early if it opens a better question; do not withhold it by rule.
vsauce.sound: Keep the spoken argument conversational and intelligible. Test a recurring musical texture that changes at genuine conceptual turns, leaving room for a difficult idea.
vsauce.typography: Introduce notation or a diagram when it helps comprehension, even before a complete verbal explanation. Cite the underlying research rather than treating the presenter as the final authority.
vsauce.exceptions: Remove automatic bans on early answers, montage and particular music. Require explicit conceptual bridges and a purposeful return to the original question.
vsauce.evaluation: Make a 30-second two-connection essay. Viewers should explain why each connection belongs and how the ending changes the opening question.
vsauce.failureMode: Unrelated trivia with rhetorical questions resembles curiosity without forming an argument.

evidence.summary: Stevens describes writing a full script, then rehearsing and delivering it in conversational paragraphs. He also directs readers toward the underlying sources. The apparent spontaneity therefore coexists with structured preparation.

sources.title: Michael Stevens Reddit AMA Transcript
sources.supports: Complete scripting, conversational paragraph delivery and pointing to underlying sources.

mark-rober.name: Mark Rober
mark-rober.reference: Engineering spectacle with accessible scientific explanation; use a specific experiment or build reference.
mark-rober.mechanism: A playful objective becomes a visible engineering problem and a satisfying test.
mark-rober.prerequisites: A real build, measurable constraints, documented iterations and coverage of a valid test.
mark-rober.selection: Choose an ambitious but legible objective and the engineering obstacle that matters most. Include an actual design decision and its consequence; omit decorative workshop footage that explains nothing.
mark-rober.framing: Establish the apparatus and test conditions clearly. Capture normal-speed cause and effect before using a close-up or slow-motion replay to reveal the mechanism.
mark-rober.rhythm: Try goal → constraint → design choice → test → explanation of result. Compress routine fabrication but preserve the decision that makes the solution understandable.
mark-rober.sound: Use music to support anticipation around the test. Let the device's real sound carry the event where useful; add a replay cue only if it helps identify a newly visible detail.
mark-rober.typography: Draw the mechanism at the moment viewers need it. Label measured results and relevant conditions; keep a simplified schematic distinct from a precise technical drawing.
mark-rober.exceptions: Remove mandatory failure, mandatory slow-motion success and fixed narration limits. Authentic progression is the requirement; the footage determines the available arc.
mark-rober.evaluation: Create a 30-second build story with one constraint and one design response. Viewers should explain why the design improved the result.
mark-rober.failureMode: A spectacular payoff with no understandable design choice becomes a stunt rather than engineering storytelling.

evidence.summary: The Stanford event report records Rober discussing science embedded in entertaining storytelling and the value of authenticity. It supports accessible engineering narratives, not a requirement to fabricate a failed attempt or slow every successful result.

sources.title: YouTuber and former NASA engineer Mark Rober draws full crowd, speaks to scientific storytelling
sources.author_publisher: Jack Quach and Steven D. Liu, The Stanford Daily
sources.evidence_type: Firsthand event reporting with direct quotations
sources.supports: Entertainment as a route into science and the importance of authentic storytelling.

emma-chamberlain.name: Emma Chamberlain
emma-chamberlain.reference: Personal vlog and editorial self-observation; identify a period rather than freezing the creator in an early style.
emma-chamberlain.mechanism: The edit reveals the gap between a performed self and a more candid thought.
emma-chamberlain.prerequisites: Authentic first-person material, meaningful self-reaction and ordinary moments whose context is retained.
emma-chamberlain.selection: Choose a small experience with a genuine change of thought. Preserve the detail that makes it personal; avoid substituting generic awkwardness for the speaker's actual perspective.
emma-chamberlain.framing: Use proximity or a self-directed camera when it creates intimacy. Keep a wider or quiet observational shot if it contributes to the experience rather than rejecting polish automatically.
emma-chamberlain.rhythm: Test a straightforward spoken version, then add a small number of editorial asides, ellipses or reframings. Each should reveal a thought absent from the unedited delivery.
emma-chamberlain.sound: Use room sound, breath or a selective interruption to expose the moment. Music is a tonal choice; silence should feel connected to the experience rather than mechanically inserted.
emma-chamberlain.typography: Write captions as an additional thought only when that voice is authentic. Separate necessary accessibility captions from optional comic or reflective commentary.
emma-chamberlain.exceptions: Remove blanket bans on polished footage, smooth transitions and clean introductions. Label early chaotic-edit references separately from other periods.
emma-chamberlain.evaluation: Create a 25-second ordinary-life scene with two editorial interventions. Viewers should identify what those edits reveal about the speaker beyond the literal words.
emma-chamberlain.failureMode: Random zooms and self-deprecating captions imitate mannerisms without a personal point of view.

evidence.summary: Chamberlain's V Magazine interview describes enjoyment of editing, creative autonomy and limits on constant filming. It supports the importance of a personal editorial voice; comments about slowing life down should not be misreported as measured evidence of slower cutting.
evidence.basis: Direct interview; era-specific visual prescriptions proposed

sources.title: Emma Chamberlain and Derek Blasberg interview
sources.supports: Editing enjoyment, creative autonomy and boundaries around filming.

peter-mckinnon.name: Peter McKinnon
peter-mckinnon.reference: Cinematic vlog and filmmaking instruction; the 2018 Epidemic Sound BTS provides a specific workflow account.
peter-mckinnon.mechanism: Tactile supplementary footage gives an everyday activity sensory appeal and continuity.
peter-mckinnon.prerequisites: Coherent coverage of a real activity, useful detail shots and motion that can connect adjacent images.
peter-mckinnon.selection: Collect beginning, action and result alongside texture. Choose details that locate the activity or reveal a step; use beauty shots to strengthen a sequence with an actual progression.
peter-mckinnon.framing: Control light direction, reflections and foreground depth. Mix wide context, medium action and close detail; include static frames where they make texture or action easier to read.
peter-mckinnon.rhythm: Build a short action sequence before adding transitions. Match movement only where it preserves orientation or creates a purposeful reveal; keep the result on screen long enough to register.
peter-mckinnon.sound: Use captured practical sounds for tactile detail and a music phrase for overall flow. Test transitions without effects and retain accents only where they clarify or enhance the action.
peter-mckinnon.typography: Keep tutorial labels functional and title design separate from the montage. Grade for consistent material and skin rendering rather than enforcing one LUT or black level.
peter-mckinnon.exceptions: Remove compulsory camera movement, transition sounds and host-duration ceilings. Require B-roll to establish, connect, demonstrate or reveal.
peter-mckinnon.evaluation: Create a 20-second everyday-task montage. A viewer should reconstruct the action's beginning and result without narration; remove any beauty shot that breaks that logic.
peter-mckinnon.failureMode: Slow motion and whooshes can make a sequence attractive while leaving it narratively incomplete.

evidence.summary: The BTS account describes McKinnon finding structure in the timeline, using B-roll to establish scenes and bridge story gaps, and sometimes choosing music before filming and sometimes afterward. It does not support requiring movement and a sound effect on every transition.
evidence.basis: Production participant's account; commercial context disclosed

martin-scorsese.name: Martin Scorsese
martin-scorsese.reference: Goodfellas and Casino for insider seduction, social machinery and unraveling; The Irishman for retrospective restraint. Select one film/sequence as the governing reference. Credit editor Thelma Schoonmaker and the relevant camera, sound, music and title collaborators.
martin-scorsese.mechanism: An insider's account draws us into a world of status and appetite, then behavior and consequences expose the cost.
martin-scorsese.materialFit: Archive-compatible with character and consequence coverage; choreographed camera passages need suitable source footage or a shoot
martin-scorsese.prerequisites: Log a protagonist's desire, an actual transaction or ritual granting access, a change in a relationship, and its visible cost. For archive, retain dates and speaker context. For a sustained moving shot, secure a readable route, blocking, permissions, lighting and sound; a digital push-in cannot supply missing space.
martin-scorsese.selection: Tag selects as invitation, privilege, procedure, fracture or aftermath. Favor a telling exchange, money or object changing hands, someone granting access, or a listener reassessing a speaker. Retain performance turns and ordinary labor that explain how the world works. Glamour and consequences must both have concrete footage.
martin-scorsese.framing: Use proximity, eyelines, doorways and foreground obstacles to show who belongs and who controls access. For new footage, choreograph a move around changing relationships and rehearse the complete route. With existing clips, preserve their screen direction and spatial anchors. Choose light, lens contrast and palette from the named film; red light is optional.
martin-scorsese.rhythm: Build an inviting scene, compress repeated procedures, then let a specific hesitation or refusal interrupt the momentum. Vary complete dialogue scenes with associative montage. A freeze, repeated detail, temporal jump or abrupt cut needs a stated narrative job and readable duration. Preserve performance over cosmetic continuity when justified. For The Irishman, allow quiet and aftermath to dominate rather than importing Goodfellas velocity.
martin-scorsese.sound: Optional first-person narration can give a character's self-justification while picture reveals a discrepancy; write concrete recollection and avoid imitating an actor's voice. Use verified quotes for factual subjects. Audition exact song recordings/passages for emotional subtext, period and structural turns; song, score or unscored scene are valid. Map which line, lyric, practical sound or musical phrase leads each moment, with separate stems and deliberate quiet after consequences.
martin-scorsese.typography: Design the film title as a story-specific metaphor or identity, separately from supporting dates, names and quotes. Credit Saul and Elaine Bass when referencing their Casino sequence. Bundled bold sans and restrained serif treatments are editorial options, not verified Scorsese-wide fonts. Animate only when motion expresses the chosen idea; hold source labels long enough to read.
martin-scorsese.exceptions: This profile also supports restrained character drama and period work. Narration, pop songs, freeze frames, violence, red lighting and long tracking shots are optional. A trailer needs its own campaign construction and named trailer execution where available; a film-director reference is not a trailer-agency credit. Preserve factual integrity when translating the mechanism to documentary material.
martin-scorsese.evaluation: Make a 20-30-second proof with an invitation, a visible privilege or transaction, and a consequence. A viewer should identify whose perspective shaped the opening, who held power, and what changed. Test a song-led and an unscored turn; inspect geography, full dialogue, title legibility and the final hold. Report listening and material limitations separately.
martin-scorsese.failureMode: A rapid gangster montage with a familiar rock song supplies surface attitude but no social mechanism, changing point of view or cost.

Ballhaus and McConkey describe spatial planning and camera collaboration. The Casino title record credits Saul and Elaine Bass. The harness mechanism and exercise are editorial translations of these accounts.
evidence.basis: Primary collaborator interviews and reproduced production/title records; sequence-specific evidence. Production recipes and numeric defaults are editorial proposals, not measured career-wide laws.
